ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (dark) background with a high frequency of localized high-intensity (white/grey) pixels, estimated at a 15:85 ratio of light-to-dark pixel coverage.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Continuous dark pigmentation base across the entire visible surface, punctuated by a dense, non-uniform distribution of small, high-contrast annular and solid circular clusters (rosettes) ranging from 5 to 20 pixels in diameter.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, symmetrical V-shaped median notch with an interior angle of approximately 45 degrees relative to the horizontal plane of the fluke center.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations with pixel amplitudes of 3-10 pixels along the left lobe; the right lobe exhibits more jagged, coarse topography with larger indentations.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Left lobe follows a smooth convex trajectory towards the tip; right lobe exhibits a truncated, blunted sweep trajectory at the distal extremity due to tissue irregularity.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Global distribution of high-contrast white circular and semi-circular pixel clusters across both lobes, with higher spatial density observed on the right medial and distal regions.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Faint, near-vertical linear pixel disruptions visible on the mid-to-lower section of the left lobe, cutting through the dark pigmentation.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent irregular region of pigmentation loss and textured tissue exposure at the far-right distal tip, characterized by a transition to orange and pinkish pixel values, indicating significant localized trauma or lesion.
other_distinctive_markers: The localized orange-chroma patch on the right fluke tip is a highly unique visual marker contrasting the monochromatic rest of the fluke.
